verdicts.quote: A ticket is waiting on its requester while its status is `resolved`

a ticket resolved at T0 whose status is still `resolved` at T0 + REMINDER_AFTER_HOURS (default 72h) has exactly one pending `ticket.reminder` outbox event addressed to its requester after the next worker tick.
further ticks after the reminder, even once it is sent, enqueue nothing more.
a ticket reopened or closed before the threshold is not reminded.
verdicts.missing: Status changes and title edits have defined effects. The spec does not say how an off-API requester reply is recognized or who records the reopening.

verdicts.quote: `to` is the ticket's requester, `ticket` is its id, and the rendered message has subject `[<id>] Waiting on you` and a body naming the ticket title and saying it can be reopened by replying.
verdicts.missing: The body has no required wait duration. The requester field supplies the destination, but handling a value that is not a deliverable address is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: a body naming the ticket title and saying it can be reopened by replying.
the check is a job of the worker; no timer of its own and no request does it. … the job scans all tickets each tick
at most one event per (ticket, resolve time) key, before and after restart
verdicts.missing: The invariant prevents duplicate events. It leaves open how to prevent a second delivery if a send succeeds and the worker retries that same event.

verdicts.quote: a ticket that is open, in_progress or closed is never reminded, however old.
verdicts.missing: The eligibility rule is explicit, but the spec does not require checking the current status and resolved period at enqueue time if the ticket changed after the scan.

verdicts.quote: delivery follows the outbox rules unchanged (retry with backoff, dead after 5).
verdicts.missing: The one-event-per-period rule also covers a dead event. The spec does not say whether enqueueing requires a registered template.

verdicts.quote: resolved at T0 and first tick at T0 + 167h gives one reminder; first tick at T0 + 168h and at T0 + 10 days gives none.
reminded again 72h after the new resolve, not before. … at most one event per (ticket, resolve time) key, before and after restart
at T0 + 71h59m no reminder; at exactly T0 + 72h a reminder (threshold is inclusive).
verdicts.missing: The spec names the test clock but leaves the production clock source, time zone and treatment of nonbusiness hours, weekends and holidays unstated.

verdicts.quote: no new stored ticket field; the reminder lives in the outbox and persists with it. Invariant: at most one event per (ticket, resolve time) key, before and after restart
verdicts.missing: The spec identifies the resolve-time audit field and the outbox record, but does not name the persisted outbox field that carries the resolve time or composite key through save and reload.

verdicts.quote: the data file format (version 1; old files load) … a test that loads a data file with no reminder events.
verdicts.missing: Old-file behavior is defined. The spec does not require rejecting malformed reminder data on load with a message naming the offending field.

verdicts.quote: A reminder is not a ticket change: no audit entry, `updated` unchanged.
no UI, no new input or endpoint
verdicts.missing: The environment setting and endpoint exclusion constrain the controls, but the spec does not identify who may configure reminders or whether existing admin facilities allow a manual send or stop.

verdicts.quote: a number greater than 0 and less than 168, the reply window of R-1; default 72 … stops start with a message naming `REMINDER_AFTER_HOURS` … `WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=0` turns reminders off with the rest of the background work.
a notifier test reading the NOTIFY_FILE line.
verdicts.missing: The delivery file provides a record of sends. The spec does not say how operators see upcoming reminders or whether the CLI preserves its raw column positions.

verdicts.quote: the job scans all tickets each tick; at current size acceptable, no numeric bound invented.
verdicts.missing: R-1 ties enqueueing to the next tick. There is no delivery-lateness bound, per-tick enqueue limit or requirement to keep a large scan from blocking delivery.

verdicts.quote: Created and resolved notifications, the lifecycle table, API responses, the audit log, the data file format (version 1; old files load) and the existing 117 tests are unchanged.
verdicts.missing: The preservation clause does not specify list-filter behavior or the output of the command line and weekly report.

verdicts.quote: CHANGELOG section and version bump (1.5.0), README config row, docs/operations.md note, ADR 0009 for the reminder design
verdicts.missing: The spec calls for manual-clock tests and names the other documentation changes, but does not require an API documentation update.
